newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seventy-one in major French paedophilia trial.
newsitem.headline: Seventy-one in major French paedophilia trial.

text.p: France's first major paedophilia trial opened in Paris on Monday with 71 Frenchmen accused of organising or subscribing to a network selling pornographic films involving boys.
The alleged organisers face up to 10 years in prison for corrupting minors. The accused clients, the bulk of the defendants, are liable to up to five years as accomplices.
The defendants included 45-year-old Jean-Manuel Willaume who is accused of shooting the films in Colombia with local boys for a company called Toro Bravo (Wild Bull). He has denied the charges.
Others stand accused of editing the films and selling them as videocassettes through advertisements in pornographic magazines.
The alleged customers for films such as "Little John I", "Little John II" or "Carlos" were arrested in a series of swoops last year and released pending trial.
The presiding judge, Sophie Portier, said they were from all social classes and from all regions of the country.
One of the defendants questioned on Monday said he had not known the boys in the films were aged under 18.
The judges are expected to be shown the cassettes at a hearing behind closed doors. The trial is expected to last two weeks.
